correctness.rationale: For normalized Bergman monomials, explicit shift weights, radial diagonal entries and the selfcommutator normalization give the stated \(b_n\)(s). The exact rational inequality at \(s=1/2\) proves every bond <=s/2 for all \(s\ge1/2\). For 0<\(s<1/2\), \(b_n\)=(s/2)(1+(1/2-s)/n+O(\(n^{-2}\))); the exact quadratic form gives Coulomb potential V_n=s(1/2-s)/n+O(\(n^{-2}\)). Geometric Dirichlet/Neumann block bracketing, finite-rank cut errors and an explicitly evaluated integral prove the sharp counting law, from which simple paired eigenvalues and \(n^{-2}\) law follow. The standalone standard-library checker passed 4631 exact and supplementary finite tests; no finite experiment substitutes for the infinite min-max argument.

originality.rationale: The exact power-symbol problem and implicit normalized Jacobi criterion were already known (Simanek 2018/2020, Le–Simanek 2020), and the first-order \(1/n\) expansion of the published matrix is elementary; those parts are credited. New is an explicit exact hyponormal phase at \(s=1/2\), the dichotomy in outer eigenvalue counts, and the rigorously derived sharp \(\varepsilon^{-1/2}\) and \(n^{-2}\) constants. Actual primary material and semantic searches found no theorem asserting the combined conclusions. Historical priority and generic semiclassical derivations remain material residual risks.
residual_risks: An unindexed article or book may give an equivalent exact counting result for this Jacobi family.

value.rationale: The natural nonharmonic symbol z+C|z|^s posed a sharp hyponormal coefficient question. The result resolves the previously implicit threshold throughout the previously unsettled power range 1/2<=s<2 and identifies a sharp spectral-phase boundary as s crosses 1/2. Below it, the full exterior bound-state accumulation constant quantifies how the criterion is stricter, beyond qualitative eigenvalue existence. This is a motivated continuous family of operators and an infinite-dimensional spectral invariant, not arbitrary finite enumeration.
